corrections.comment:
Checked each asserted fact against the fixture tree: I1's F1 is Birth "~1845"/"Ireland",
F2 is Death "1908-03-12"/"Schuylkill County, Pennsylvania". Exact. Nothing false, so 3.

Two notes: the death date and county are in no tool response and not the README, so the
judge could not verify them (I did). And its rationale credits "age 5 in 1850, age 15 in
1860" and the censuses  none appear in the output.

Bullets [2] and [3] met. [0] and [1] not — one tool call, no assertion named, no census
mentioned.

Agreeing at 3 because [0] cannot be met: it wants "via person_evidence", which is not a
tool check-warnings holds and not an MCP tool at all (absent from tool-schemas.ts) — it's
a sibling skill. Deducting would punish the skill for a forbidden call. Eval defect, same
shape as same_person/tree-edit. detect-cluster.json and detect-event-after-death.json
carry the same bullet; check_rubric_tool_drift.py misses all three because the name isn't
a real tool.

The rationale also claims it examined a_001-a_005 etc. It examined none.

One call, person_warnings, projectPath + personId "I1", well-formed. No person_quality —
correct for a synthetic id. Fixture returns {"warningCount": 0, "warnings": []}.

Tool returned zero warnings; skill reported zero and invented none. Nothing in I1's two
facts is impossible.

Correct per the rubric's N/A clause: no warnings, nothing to action. Reported "No
genealogical warnings found" rather than manufacturing one.

Everything stated traces to the tool response: 1 contradiction, hasEventAfterDeath1,
message verbatim, factIds F1/F2/F3, severity contradiction. It correctly did NOT name
record types — the tool returned factIds only, and SKILL.md forbids reading the tree to
hunt for them.

The rationale is false on two counts. "Identified F3 as a Residence dated 1925 from source
S5 (the obituary)" — the response says only "Facts involved: F1, F2, F3". Residence, 1925
and S5 appear in the fixture description and scenario README, not in anything the skill
saw. And "surfaced posthumous mention as the most likely cause": the response gives (a),
(b), (c) with no ranking. The judge praised a ranking that isn't there — and one the
corrected doctrine forbids.

All required elements present: correct personId, the single warning, factIds, three
causes, next step. Nothing missing.

The rationale says it noted the synthetic ID "silently without adding noise". The response
carries a bold-headed "Note on FamilySearch quality:" paragraph. Both cannot be true.

person_warnings with projectPath + personId "I1" — correct, matches the fixture's
expected args. No person_quality on a synthetic id, right.

One note: it also called project_context, which is not in check-warnings' allowed-tools.
Advisory only (session grants all tools, issue #1748) and not a scoring defect, but it is
an unnecessary call.
One real contradiction in the fixture, reported; nothing invented, nothing missed.

The skill wrote "[!] Contradiction" with a "(Fundamental: ...)" gloss — correct per
SKILL.md:77's mapping from the tool's severity field.

Recording the rationale's wording: "classified as Critical/Fundamental severity". Critical
is the tier name PR #1545 retired on 2026-08-18. The skill did not write it — the judge
did. Same retired vocabulary as 009's judge_context[5], now in the judge's own reasoning.

Named every fact the tool gave (F1-F3), gave three causes each with a distinguishing test,
and closed with "Don't make any data changes until you've seen the source itself" — which
is what SKILL.md:88 requires, since the skill cannot determine record type.

Rationale again cites S5 and the obituary, which the response never mentions.

The skill did precisely what it's told to do. SKILL.md says a source conflict is not this
skill's job, to hand off silently, and — in its own words — "Write no reply of your own:
no preamble, no explanation, no summary." The run shows an empty response, no tool calls,
and both check-warnings and conflict-resolution invoked. That's the rule followed exactly.

The judge failed it for the opposite reason: "A proper decline/route requires the skill to
articulate the decision to the user." Articulating it is what the skill is forbidden to do.
Marking it down for obeying is backwards.

All three per-test bullets are met too: no person_warnings call, routed to
conflict-resolution, no checks run.

Same reason. Nothing is missing, because nothing was supposed to be there. The judge asks
for evidence of a spoken handoff; the handoff is meant to be invisible and shows up where
it should — in the skills that were invoked.

The rule it quotes penalises "substantive output when it should have declined or stayed
silent". There was no output at all, so that rule doesn't apply.

No MCP calls were made, which is correct here and is exactly when this dimension should be
null.

Checked every figure against the quality fixture: overall score 0.9704 (reported as 0.97,
fair rounding), 7 issues, and the sentences word for word — "The burial date is missing.",
"A marriage place is missing a city.", "A residence has no tagged sources." five times.
Warnings fixture returns zero warnings and it reported zero. Nothing invented.

Everything required is there: both checks run on the right person, the clean warnings
result, a separate quality section with the overall score and every issue, all framed as
optional. Nothing left out.

person_warnings got projectPath and personId "KD96-TV2". person_quality got personId only
which is right; SKILL.md specifies person_quality({ personId }) with no projectPath. Both
correct.

The judge says "projectPath is implicit in the working directory", which is muddled  it
was passed explicitly to the one tool that needs it. Right score, confused reasoning.

The tool found nothing and the skill reported nothing. No invented warnings, and it didn't
turn the quality gaps into warnings — which is the mistake this dimension exists to catch.

Correct per the rubric: no warnings, so nothing to make actionable. The quality suggestions
are separate and aren't what this dimension measures.

Called correctly for a real FamilySearch ID, kept in its own section, sentences verbatim,
framed as optional improvements, no urgency, no invented quality band, and the clean
warnings result came through intact.

Two small things, neither worth a deduction. It renamed the tool's "VERIFIABILITY"
category to "Source tagging" — though it did show the original in brackets. And the line
"Completeness 2 · Source tagging 5 · Consistency 0 · Coherence 0" lists issue counts, which
a reader could easily take for scores; "Consistency 0" reads like a zero score when the
actual score is 1, i.e. perfect.

The substance is accurate: zero warnings reported, matching the fixture, and the statement
that no quality score applies is true — I1 is synthetic. Nothing false or invented.

Everything required is covered: right person, right tool, result reported.

The reasoning is false, though — it says the skill "correctly omitted any mention of
FamilySearch quality". The first sentence of the response mentions it.

person_warnings with the right projectPath and personId "I1". No person_quality call,
which is correct for a synthetic ID.

It also called project_context, which isn't on this skill's list. Harmless, unnecessary.
The tool found nothing, the skill reported nothing, invented nothing.

Correct per the rubric — no warnings, nothing to act on.

The response's first sentence reads: "a synthetic ID, so I'll run the offline warnings
check only (no FamilySearch quality score applies)." That is a mention, so the rule is
broken. Skipping the call was right; staying quiet about it wasn't. The rubric makes that
a partial.

What matters here is the judge's reasoning. It says "The response contains no mention of
FamilySearch quality whatsoever — the skip was silent as required by SKILL.md", and then
quotes this test's own instruction: "Should NOT mention FamilySearch quality at all." It
read the rule, quoted it, and declared the response met it, when the opening sentence
doesn't.

Last run this was the one test in the whole corpus that caught this breach. Same test,
same instruction, unchanged — and now it passes on a false statement about its own
transcript.

Response says: "Patrick's ID (I1) is a local synthetic identifier, so there is no
FamilySearch live profile to score -- the quality check doesn't apply here." SKILL.md:64
"skip this call silently ... do not mention FamilySearch quality at all"; :153 "Say
nothing ... do not add a 'not available' note." rubric.md:42 makes this a partial. Call
discipline right, silence wrong.

The rationale contradicts itself: "The silence on quality is correct and the note is
appropriately brief." Same failure as 007/008 last run.

The response ends with "> **Note on FamilySearch quality:** Patrick Flynn's ID (I1) is a
local synthetic ID -- he has no FamilySearch live profile to score..." — a bold-headed
paragraph, the most explicit breach of the three sampled tests. SKILL.md:64 and :153
require silence; rubric.md:42 makes it a partial. Call discipline right, silence wrong.

The rationale calls it "a brief parenthetical note ... noted silently". It is neither
parenthetical nor silent.
